sisterShips: Costa neoRomantica (ex-Costa Romantica; sold to Celestyal in 2020, renamed Antares Experience, scrapped at Gadani, Pakistan in December 2021 — no longer sailing)

zones.what: Deck 10 (Exuma/Portofino Deck) houses cruise cabins from 1001 to 1010, all midship-located Grand Terrace Suites, and also carries the ship's service boats (6 tenders, 8 lifeboats), and a first-hand visitor account reports the buffet dining area's windows had an obstructed view, with lifeboats blocking what would otherwise be a water view.
zones.effect: Diners in the buffet (fore/aft ends of Deck 10) look out at boat hulls instead of open water; the Grand Terrace Suites, which sit midship on the same deck, are not described as obstructed in any first-hand cabin review found.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone picking a buffet-adjacent window seat expecting an open sea view; does not appear to matter to Grand Terrace Suite bookers, whose balcony reviews describe open, unobstructed views.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com deck-10 plan page (boat stowage + suite location) and outandback.live first-hand blog (buffet window obstruction)

zones.what: The License to Chill pool deck sits one deck above the Grand Terrace Suites, and even in the ship's Grand Terrace suite on Deck 10, reviewers still heard quite a bit of noise from the pool deck above, with crew pulling out deck chairs every morning.
zones.effect: The top cabin deck's most expensive rooms get an early-morning wake-up from chair-dragging on the pool deck directly overhead, despite being the 'premium' product on the ship.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to suite guests who want to sleep in; less relevant to guests on lower decks 4-7 who are insulated from this by several public decks in between.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Margaritaville at Sea Paradise Cabins & Suites editor review (first-hand stay in a Grand Terrace Suite)

zones.what: On this hull, Deck 5 is the second lowest deck with passenger cabins, with the Atrium, reception, tour office and a small chapel situated amidships; the five-deck-high Atrium begins on Deck 5 and reaches Deck 9, which is why the per-deck data shows almost no midship cabins on Decks 5-6 and only a partial midship pocket reappearing on Deck 7 as the atrium void narrows higher up.
zones.effect: Midship cabins on Decks 5 and 6 are squeezed to a handful (or zero) because the multi-deck atrium/lobby occupies that footprint; guests in the few midship cabins that do exist there are close to lobby foot traffic, the reception desk, and stairs/lifts serving the atrium.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests sensitive to lobby noise and elevator/stair traffic; a non-issue for forward or aft cabins on the same decks, which are structurally separated from the atrium well.
zones.source: cruisewonderland.tiyogami.com Costa Classica ship tour (same hull, pre-rename, deck-by-deck architectural description)

zones.what: A ship-specific cabin guide warns that lower aft cabins on Deck 4 have porthole-only windows and proximity to the engine room on a 35-year-old ship, meaning vibration is a real issue, consistent with the class's 4 × diesel engines on 2 shafts propulsion arrangement typically housed low and aft.
zones.effect: Guests in aft Deck 4 oceanview/interior cabins may feel low-frequency engine hum/vibration, especially at higher cruising speeds or rough seas.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and vibration-sensitive travelers; not a concern for forward or midship cabins on Deck 4, or for any cabins on Decks 5-7 and 10.
zones.source: planetpatrick.net 'Best Cabins on Margaritaville Paradise' cabin guide

zones.what: A ship-specific cabin guide separately flags cabins adjacent to the central atrium, noting the atrium on a 1991-built ship does not have the acoustic separation of modern designs, so corridor and common-area noise carries at night, and a Cruise Critic editor's stay in a Deck 5 oceanview cabin found a ton of hallway noise... even with the door closed, conversations from across-the-hall neighbors carried through.
zones.effect: Thin cabin walls/doors on this 1991-built hull let hallway and neighbor conversation through even with doors shut, independent of proximity to any single noisy venue.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone wanting a quiet room regardless of deck; this appears to be a ship-wide construction-era trait rather than a location-specific one.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Paradise Cabins editor review + planetpatrick.net cabin guide

zones.what: A cabin guide describes the midship Deck 10 Grand Terrace Suite position as the most stable point on the ship at sea, while Cruise Critic's own editors advise that if you're prone to seasickness, you'll want to pick a room in the middle of the ship on a lower deck.
zones.effect: Motion is felt least in midship cabins on the lower-numbered guest decks (4-6) and in the midship Deck 10 suites; forward and aft cabins, and cabins on higher decks generally, will roll and pitch more in swell.
zones.mattersTo: Matters most to first-time cruisers or anyone prone to seasickness choosing between forward/aft oceanview cabins versus midship options.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Paradise editor review + planetpatrick.net cabin guide

zones.what: CruiseMapper's cabin inventory notes the ship has no connecting (family) or Spa cabins, and separately that there are 6 wheelchair-accessible cabins aboard.
zones.effect: Families needing two adjoining rooms cannot book connecting cabins on this ship at all, unlike many newer ships; accessible cabins are limited in number fleet-wide.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to families/groups wanting adjoining rooms and to wheelchair users needing to confirm specific accessible cabin locations before booking.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com Margaritaville At Sea Paradise cabins and suites page

zones.what: Multiple sources confirm Paradise doesn't have traditional balcony cabins at all; it jumps straight from an Oceanview cabin to a Junior Suite, and only the Grand Terrace Suite tier has an outdoor balcony — the mid-range balcony category found on most other cruise lines does not exist on this ship.
zones.effect: There is no 'standard balcony' price point to book; guests wanting any private outdoor space must pay the full suite premium for one of the 10 Grand Terrace Suites.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to shoppers used to a balcony/oceanview/interior three-tier structure; budget-balcony seekers will not find that option here at any price.
zones.source: famvia.com room-options guide + planetpatrick.net cabin guide

leads.cabins: Deck 4, aft, oceanview/interior (exact numbers not given)
leads.claim: Lower aft Deck 4 cabins are called out by name as having engine-room-proximity vibration issues on this 35-year-old ship.
leads.source: planetpatrick.net 'Best Cabins on Margaritaville Paradise, and Why'

leads.claim: Even in the top-tier suite, reviewers heard pool-deck noise (crew dragging deck chairs) from the deck directly above every morning.
leads.source: cruisecritic.com Margaritaville at Sea Paradise Cabins & Suites editor review

leads.cabins: Deck 5 oceanview (specific cabin number not given)
leads.claim: Thin walls/doors let hallway conversation and foot traffic noise through clearly, despite being far from the pool.
leads.source: cruisecritic.com Margaritaville at Sea Paradise Cabins & Suites editor review

leads.cabins: Buffet-area window seats, Deck 10 (High Tide Market / Port of Indecision Buffet, not guest cabins)
leads.claim: Buffet windows on Deck 10 have an obstructed, lifeboat-blocked view rather than open water.
Cabin walls lack soft wall coverings, producing a noticeable cold echo/acoustic bounce inside the room.

unknowns: No source found describing a 'hump' (cantilevered balcony) feature on this hull; given the ship's 1991 vintage and that only 10 midship suites have any balcony at all, a hump is unlikely but not confirmed either way.
No source found describing hull taper effects at the top of the ship (Deck 10 suites are midship, where taper is least likely to matter, but this was not directly confirmed).
No source found on the specific location of the crew-only 'I-95'-style corridor or its service-access points relative to guest cabins on Decks 4-7.
No source found confirming bow thruster noise or anchor-chain noise for forward Deck 4 cabins specifically, despite Deck 4 forward being the most likely candidate structurally.
No source gives exact cabin numbers for the 6 wheelchair-accessible cabins or confirms which decks they are on.

Whether Deck 6 and Deck 7 midship cabins (30 on Deck 7 per the inventory) are close enough to the atrium void to experience the same noise reported on Deck 5 was not independently confirmed by a first-hand review.
